extracted.intended_audience: Physician-scientist applicants for NIH K08 (Mentored Clinical Scientist Research Career Development) awards, their mentors, and institutional grant administrators
extracted.subtask_description: An NIH review summary statement for a K08 resubmission evaluating overall impact and the standard review criteria (Candidate; Career Development Plan; Research Plan; Mentors; Environment) plus human subjects, biosafety, and administrative items. It summarizes strengths, weaknesses, and administrative determinations relevant to funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact / Priority Score
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall Impact/Priority score assessing the likelihood that the project will exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The impact/priority score is calculated after discussion by averaging overall scores (1-9) given by all voting reviewers and multiplying by 10. Criterion scores are submitted prior to the meeting by individual reviewers and are not discussed specifically at the review meeting or calculated into the overall impact score. Some applications also receive a percentile ranking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Candidate (Qualifications and Productivity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the applicant's training, expertise, and track record (e.g., MD/PhD, clinical training, prior fellowship, publication record).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate whether the candidate is well prepared for the proposed career development step, including prior publications (>20 manuscripts noted), relevant training in infectious diseases, immunology, and bioinformatics, and commitment (e.g., protected research time). Strengths and any minor weaknesses (e.g., writing style in abstract) are noted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Career Development Plan / Career Goals / Plan to Provide Mentoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the training plan and mentoring proposed to develop the candidate's independence and skills (didactic and hands-on training, tutorials, mentoring structure).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider alignment of long- and short-term goals with the applicant's background, adequacy of planned coursework/training (e.g., biostatistics, computational modeling), feasibility of timeline (e.g., plan to submit R01 in Year 4-5), and quality of mentor involvement. Training in Responsible Conduct of Research (format, subject matter, faculty participation, duration) is part of this assessment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Research Plan (Significance, Approach, Rigor, Feasibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of the scientific merit of the research plan including aims, methods, and overall strategy to achieve the stated goals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate appropriateness of approaches (e.g., systems biology + multi-parameter modeling), use of cohorts/specimens, proposed assays (transcriptomics, flow cytometry, cytokines, Pf-specific IgG), and statistical/machine learning methods. Specific concerns flagged include questionable rigor and statistical power, under-powered sample sizes for extensive 'omics' testing, insufficient handling of host genetic background, lack of discussion of interaction/pathway analyses (mechanistic insight vs predictors), challenges in interpreting machine learning 'black box' outputs, potential logistical pitfalls (loss of access to study population; absence of backup site), and technical feasibility (e.g., feasibility of obtaining sufficient RNA-seq reads from fingerstick). Strengths include appropriate methodology and potential to provide candidate training.

rubrics_metrics.name: Mentor(s), Co-Mentor(s), Consultant(s), Collaborator(s)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the qualifications, complementary expertise, and commitment of the mentoring and collaborator team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether mentors provide the expertise needed (e.g., primary mentor with continuous NIH funding, co-mentors in biostatistics and computational biology, NIAID mentor), and whether collaborators provide necessary resources. Reviewers note strengths (well-qualified team) and may flag concerns about mentorship quality if project design deficiencies persist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment and Institutional Commitment to the Candidate
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of institutional resources, facilities, protected time, and demonstrated commitment to support the candidate's development.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate adequacy of resources (lab space, equipment), institutional commitment (tenure-track offer, 80% protected research time), and availability of patient samples or cohort data. Reviewers may assess whether environment matches the needs of proposed training (e.g., bioinformatics resources).

rubrics_metrics.name: Protection of Human Subjects
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of human subjects protections and classification (e.g., Exempt Human Subjects Research: use of existing specimens and clinical data).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure proposed human-subjects work conforms to NIH policies (PHS398 materials and NIH OER guidance). Exemption codes (e.g., E4) and justification for exempt status must be documented. Consideration includes use of existing 'in-the-freezer' specimens, privacy, and data handling procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Women
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan for inclusion of women in the research or justification if not applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For exempt studies using existing specimens/data, indicate applicability. Plans or justifications should conform to NIH inclusion policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Minorities
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan for inclusion of racial and ethnic minorities or justification if not applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Document whether the study population and data allow assessment across relevant groups and follow NIH inclusion policies; exemptions must be justified similarly to other inclusion criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Children
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan for inclusion of children in the research or justification if not applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When children are the population of interest (e.g., Malian children cohort), ensure NIH inclusion policies for children are addressed; exempt status should be explicitly justified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of vertebrate animal use and compliance with policies (Code: e.g., 10 - Not applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: State that no vertebrate animals will be used if applicable; if animals are used, provide appropriate protocol and justification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazard Comment
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of biohazard risks and whether adequate biosafety measures are addressed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Biohazard handling must be described; in this summary 'BIOHAZARD COMMENT: UNACCEPTABLE' was recorded because 'No biohazards were addressed.' Applicants must address biohazard concerns in proposals where relevant.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission Responsiveness
rubrics_metrics.description: Assessment of how well the resubmitted application addresses prior reviewer concerns and whether revisions strengthened the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers evaluate modifications (e.g., combining aims, new Aim 2) and whether prior criticisms (e.g., lack of host genetic analysis, scope, statistical methods) were sufficiently addressed. Resubmissions should explicitly summarize changes and justify remaining choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Training in the Responsible Conduct of Research (RCR)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation of the proposed RCR training (format, subject matter, faculty participation, duration, frequency).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess acceptability of RCR plan (e.g., format: online & classroom; subject matter: conflicts of interest, misconduct, authorship, ethics; duration: 22.5 contact hours; faculty involvement) and whether it meets NIH expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Foreign Institution Justification
rubrics_metrics.description: Justification for involvement of foreign institutions and description of collaborator roles and access to resources (e.g., samples, cohorts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Foreign collaborations must be justified (e.g., collaborator provides access to Kalifabougou cohort samples). Document agreements, access to specimens/data, and roles of foreign collaborators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources
rubrics_metrics.description: Plan for authentication of critical reagents, specimens, and resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess whether adequate plans exist to authenticate key resources; in this summary it was judged 'ACCEPTABLE.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans / Data Sharing / Genomic Data Sharing (GDS)
rubrics_metrics.description: Plans for sharing data, model organisms, and genomic data as required (or notation if not applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must include resource sharing plans when applicable (e.g., if >$500,000/year certain data sharing comments apply). In this application some items were 'NOT APPLICABLE' but reviewers note expectations when thresholds are met.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation and recommendation regarding requested budget and award period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although the summary shows the requested budget, NIAID grants management staff will calculate final costs based on committee budget recommendations if an award is planned. In this case 'The budget was recommended as requested.'

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agents
rubrics_metrics.description: Statement on whether select agents are involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Declare applicability; in this summary 'SELECT AGENTS: NOT APPLICABLE.' If select agents are relevant, appropriate compliance documentation is required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring and Review Process Notes
rubrics_metrics.description: Procedural note on how scores are submitted and used in calculating overall impact, and how percentiles may be derived.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Criterion scores are submitted prior to the meeting by assigned reviewers and are not discussed at the meeting nor directly calculated into the overall impact score. The impact score is based on averaged overall scores after discussion. See NIH peer review process guidance for details.
